name: Kingdom of Iberia (Caucasian Iberia)
alt: Iberian Kingdom of the Pharnavazids, Artaxiads and Chosroids

successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: Iberia under Persian rule after the Eternal Peace of 532 ('Sasanians retained Iberia')

ledger.x: c. 302 BC: Pharnavaz I founds the Kingdom of Iberia. 'Pharnavaz, victorious in a power struggle, became the first king of Iberia (c. 302 - c. 237 BC)'; infobox 'c. 302 BC'. The page names the capital sites (Armazi, Mtskheta), not a boundary.
502: Vakhtang I falls in battle and the uprising ends.
523: the Iberians under Gurgen rise against Persia.
532: the Eternal Peace leaves Iberia to Persia.
533: Iberia ends as a kingdom on the map.

wars.name: Pompey's Caucasian campaign (Third Mithridatic War)
wars.outcome: Iberia is drawn into the invasion: 'drew Iberia into a Roman invasion in 65 BC' and is listed as a Roman Republic client 65-63 BC; no land changes hands on the page.

wars.name: Roman campaign in Iberia and Albania (36 BC)
wars.outcome: 'in 36 BC, Roman forces again marched into Iberia' and forced Pharnavaz II into a campaign against Albania; no territorial result.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of the Caucasus
wars.outcome: Iberia becomes a Sasanian tributary: 'During the reign of Shapur I (241-272), Iberia became a tributary of the Sasanian Empire'.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian war of 296-299 (Peace of Nisibis)
wars.outcome: 'Transfer of suzerainty of Iberia to the Roman Empire and relinquishment of the right to appoint the Iberian kings'; the Tigris becomes the frontier.

wars.name: Peace of Acilisene (387)
wars.outcome: Confirms 'Varaz-Bakur I as a Persian vassal' in Iberia; no land changes.

wars.name: Vakhtang I's uprising against Persia
wars.outcome: 'a twenty-year struggle for independence' that ends with Vakhtang's death in 502.

wars.name: Iberian War
wars.outcome: 'Sasanians retained Iberia; Byzantines retained Lazica'; the Eternal Peace of 532 returns every territory seized in the war and Byzantium pays 11,000 lbs of gold.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line is given for Iberia on any page opened; the Nisibis (299) and Acilisene (387) settlements change suzerainty, not a described frontier.
